title: Marketing at early startups: go deep on one channel you already understand
summary: Jason argues early startups should not spread thin across many marketing channels. Successful companies find one channel that works and exhaust it before adding others. Pick that channel from the few you personally use and understand, because social channel success depends on natural resonance with its culture.

principles.text: Early startups rarely win by spreading small efforts across many channels; trickles from each don't add up to a river.
principles.quote: Spreading your precious money and even more precious time over many channels doesn't get a company off the ground.

principles.text: Find one channel that really works and exhaust its maximum inventory before layering on more channels.
principles.quote: Typically, successful companies find **one channel that really works**, and then plumb it to its [maximum inventory](https://longform.asmartbear.com/low-budget-marketing/) before layering on additional channels.

principles.text: Choose your first channel from the handful you personally use and understand, not by spray and pray.
principles.quote: Start with the handful of channels that you *personally use and understand*.

principles.text: Social channel success comes from resonance between your personality and the channel's norms and language.
principles.quote: success in social marketing channels arises from a resonance between your personality and the norms and language of that channel.

principles.text: Authentic resonance arises naturally; you can't A/B test your way into a persona on a channel you don't get.
principles.quote: The best chance you have for developing that resonance is when it arises naturally, not because you A/B test your Twitter persona

principles.text: Stay in your comfort zone and focus on doubling the business on that one channel; spreading thin is worse than leaving it.
principles.quote: So, stay with what you know, where you're comfortable, and focus on doubling your business on that channel.
